direct_claims: This chart is about what kinds of information people want included in app notifications.
It compares responses from deaf participants and hard-of-hearing participants for seven information types: identity, location, volume, length, pitch, urgency, and confidence.
The possible response levels were absolutely essential, very important, moderately important, of little importance, and not important at all.
The chart comes from a paper published at ASSETS in 2016.
The chart suggests that identity, location, urgency, and confidence were more often considered at least moderately important than volume, length, and pitch.
Deaf and hard-of-hearing responses were reported as very similar, which implies the two groups may share broadly similar notification information priorities in this study.
The metadata supports only qualitative interpretation, not precise percentages or exact group differences.
The image appears to show paired bars for each information type, one for deaf participants and one for hard-of-hearing participants.
Without the underlying data table, any claim about exact rankings, percentage gaps, or effect sizes would be uncertain.
